'''Molde Fotballklubb''' ({{IPA|no|ˈmɔ̂ɫdə|-|Molde.ogg}}) is a [[association football|football]] club based in [[Molde Municipality|Molde]], [[Norway]], that competes in [[Eliteserien]], the top flight of [[Norwegian football league system|Norwegian football]]. Founded on 19 June 1911, the club was originally known as '''International''' and changed its name to Molde in 1915. Molde is five-time league champions (2011, 2012, 2014, 2019 and 2022) and six-time [[Norwegian Cup]] winner (1994, 2005, 2013, 2014, 2022 and 2023), and has finished second in the league a further eleven times. Molde is one of only four Norwegian clubs to have participated in the [[UEFA Champions League]].

The club's home matches are played at the 11,249-capacity [[Aker Stadion]].<ref name="capacity">{{cite web |url=https://www.moldefk.no/AkerStadion |language=no |title=Aker Stadion |website=moldefk.no |publisher=Molde FK |access-date=28 July 2019 |archive-date=30 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230025127/https://www.moldefk.no/AkerStadion |url-status=live }}</ref> The stadium was inaugurated in 1998, and was a gift from local businessmen [[Kjell Inge Røkke]] and [[Bjørn Rune Gjelsten]]. The club was formerly based at [[Molde Idrettspark|Molde stadion]], which hosted the club's record attendance of 6,615. Molde's supporter club is called ''Tornekrattet'' ("Thicket of thorns", a reference to the city's nickname "The Town of Roses") and was founded after the [[1994 Norwegian Football Cup final|1994 Norwegian Cup final]] victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tornekrattet.no/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=13&Itemid=56 |language=no |title=Info om Krattet |publisher=Tornekrattet |access-date=24 February 2012 |archive-date=4 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204035819/http://www.tornekrattet.no/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=13&Itemid=56 |url-status=live }}</ref> Molde has its strongest rivalry with [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]].

Until the beginning of the 1970s, the club mainly played in local lower division leagues, except for a short visit in the [[Hovedserien]] in the [[1957–58 Norwegian Main League|1957–58]] season. In [[1974 1. divisjon|1974]], Molde was back in the top division and finished second in the league, and have since then become one of Norway's leading clubs and generally stayed in the top division. Molde also finished second in the league in [[1987 1. divisjon|1987]], when the club lost the championship to [[Moss FK|Moss]] in the decisive match of the season.

During the 1990s and the beginning of the 2000s, Molde was the second-best team in Norway (behind 13-times in a row champions [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]]), with league silver medals in [[1995 Tippeligaen|1995]], [[1998 Tippeligaen|1998]], [[1999 Tippeligaen|1999]] and [[2002 Tippeligaen|2002]], and cup championships in [[1994 Norwegian Football Cup|1994]] and [[2005 Norwegian Football Cup|2005]], as well as participation in the UEFA Champions League in the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|1999–2000 season]], when [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], [[FC Porto|Porto]] and [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] visited Molde.

As of 2017, the club has approximately 1,000 members and around 55 teams in three departments.<ref name="klubbfakta">{{cite web |url=http://www.moldefk.no/om-klubben/klubbfakta |language=no |title=Molde Fotballklubb – Klubbfakta |publisher=Molde FK |access-date=10 November 2017 |archive-date=10 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110224903/http://www.moldefk.no/om-klubben/klubbfakta |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Martin Falk]] has been interim manager of the club since December 2025; he will be replaced by [[Sindre Tjelmeland]] in May 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sindre Tjelmeland og Martin Falk klare for Molde FK |url=https://www.moldefk.no/nyheter/sindre-tjelmeland-og-martin-falk-klare-for-molde-fk |publisher=moldefk.no/ |access-date=21 December 2025 |language=no |date=21 December 2025}}</ref>
